questions.q: What does a data-driven subscription do differently from a standard subscription?
options: It queries a subscriber database at run time to determine recipients, delivery settings, and parameter values
It skips the delivery extension entirely and writes straight to a database
It requires no report parameters at all
It can only be scheduled to run once, never on a recurring basis
questions.explain: A data-driven subscription's whole point is that recipients, delivery settings, and parameters come from a live query result rather than being fixed at creation time.

questions.q: What must you supply before you can define a data-driven subscription's query?
options: A Windows file share account
A shared schedule
A dataset — a data source plus the query or command that will supply the subscription's values
A pre-built list of recipient e-mail addresses in a text file
questions.explain: The wizard's Dataset section requires you to select Edit Dataset and supply a data source and query before the Query section becomes usable.

questions.q: In a data-driven subscription's query result set, what do the rows determine?
options: The schedule the subscription runs on
The report's rendering format
Which fields can be mapped to delivery settings
How many separate report deliveries get generated — one per row
questions.explain: Rows in the result set drive delivery count directly: 10,000 rows means 10,000 generated notifications and deliveries.

questions.q: In that same query result set, what do the columns determine?
options: Whether the subscription is standard or data-driven
The query timeout value
What you're allowed to map to delivery options and report parameters
How many deliveries get generated
questions.explain: Columns determine what values are available to map — an e-mail data-driven subscription, for example, needs a column of e-mail addresses to map to the To field.

questions.q: Why does Microsoft recommend running the query in SQL Server Management Studio before pasting it into the subscription wizard?
options: Because the wizard cannot run any query longer than 10 seconds
Because the wizard doesn't support SELECT statements
Because Management Studio is required to save the subscription
So you can verify the results look right and contain what you need, before debugging it inside the wizard's more limited interface
questions.explain: Testing the query separately first lets you confirm its columns and row count are correct, which is far easier to debug outside the subscription wizard.
